Meet The Speakers

Stergios Chatzikyriakidis

Professor

Stergios Chatzikyriakidis is Professor of Computational Linguistics at the Department of Philology, University of Crete, where he directs the Computational Linguistics and Language Technology Lab. He is also Head of Research at MuVeS AI and founder of SimasiaAI. His work lies at the intersection of NLP, formal semantics and type theory, the reasoning and evaluation of large language models, Computatonal Dialectology and low-resource varieties. He holds an MSc and a PhD from King’s College London.

Antonis Dimakis

PhD researcher and academic fellow at Archimedes Unit, Athena RC

Antonis Dimakis received his bachelor’s degree from the Department of Informatics and Telecommunications of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, with specializations in the Foundations of Computer Science and Data and Knowledge Management. He has since been pursuing a PhD on Natural Language Processing at the same university and is a fellow at Archimedes Unit, Athena RC. He has experience working on low-resource languages, machine translation and evaluation.

Dimitris Galanis

Principal Researcher

Dimitris Galanis holds a Ph.D. in Natural Language Processing (Nov. 2006 – Feb. 2012, title: “Automatic Generation of Natural Language Summaries”), an M.Sc. in Computer Science and a B.Sc. in Informatics. All the aforementioned degrees were obtained in the Department of Informatics at Athens University of Economics and Business. He started working at Institute for Language and Speech Processing/ “Athena” R.C in April of 2013 as a collaborating Researcher / Software Engineer and from September 2019 he is an elected Researcher. He has participated in several research projects (CLARIN:EL, OpenMinTeD, ELRC-SHARE, ELG, Language Data Space etc.). Dimitris has published papers in prominent conferences and journals that are cited more than 5000 times (according to Google Scholar). His research interests focus on Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, LLMs, and Language Resource Infrastructures.

Basilis Gatos

Research Director

Basilis G. Gatos received his Electrical Engineering Diploma and Ph.D. degree in Optical Character Recognition Techniques from the Democritus University of Thrace, Greece. He currently serves as a Researcher at the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications of NCSR “Demokritos” in Athens, Greece, and is a co-founder of the spin-off companies AI4Doc and Astros Intelligence. His professional career spans leadership roles in R&D at Lambrakis Press Archives, Computer Logic S.A., and BSI S.A. With research interests focused on Image Processing, Document Image Analysis, OCR, and Pattern Recognition, Dr. Gatos has authored over 200 publications in international journals and conference proceedings and participated in numerous EU-funded research programs. A member of the Technical Chamber of Greece, he regularly serves on program committees for major international conferences (such as ICDAR, ICFHR, and DAS) and co-organized ICFHR 2014, DAS 2016, and ICDAR 2024 in Greece.

Vassilis Katsouros

Research Director and Director of ILSP/ATHENA RC

Vassilis Katsouros is Research Director at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) of the Athena Research Center (ATHENA RC) and Director of ILSP since June 2019. He received his M.Eng. degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), Greece, in 1992. In 1993 he obtained the M.Sc. with distinction in Communications and Signal Processing from Imperial College, University of London, UK and in 1997 he received his Ph.D. degree in Mathematical modelling and Stochastic Control from Imperial College. Since 1998 he has been working at the ILSP. He is member of the Board at Athena Research Center since 2017 and member of the Board at the Information Society S.A. since June 2019. He has coordinated several research and innovation projects at national and European frameworks. His research interests involve digital signal processing, statistics analysis, machine learning and artificial intelligence with applications in a wide variety of signals and data (document, voice, music, image, video, sensorial data, etc.) He also leads ILSP’s strategic initiative for Greek LLMs, including the development of Meltemi and Krikri, the first open LLMs designed to support and advance the Greek language in the AI era.

Stella Markantonatou

Emeritus Research Director

Dr. Stella Markantonatou holds an MA in Chemical Engineering (NTUA 1983), BA in Linguistics (NKUA 1988) and a PhD in Linguistics (University of Essex 1992). She is an Emeritus Research Director at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing/ATHENA RC and a Principal Researcher in the AI Unit Archimedes/ATHENA RC. Her expertise lies in NLP for under-resourced language varieties with a focus on Modern Greek dialects and idiomatic speech, in language resource development and in knowledge representation.

Kanella Pouli

Scientific Associate

Kanella Pouli holds a BSc in Linguistics from the University of Athens and an MSc in Language Technology from the University of Athens and the National Technical University of Athens. She has been a Scientific Associate at ILSP/Athena RC since 2012 and has contributed to the following European and national projects: QTLaunchPad, CEF-ELRC, FutureTDM, ELRC+L2, CRACKER, ISD, CLARIN:EL, Apollonis, ELE, LDS, LLMs4EU, and AltEdic4EU. Her work focuses on the evaluation, usability, and continuous improvement of research infrastructures for language resources and technologies. As a research infrastructure specialist, she contributes to user-centred design, testing, and quality assurance. She also develops technical documentation and training materials and supports users through workshops, seminars, and training sessions.

Dimitris Roussis

Scientific Associate

Dimitris Roussis is a Scientific Associate and Data Scientist at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) of Athena Research Center, and co-founder of Layer42 Labs. He holds an MSc in Data Science and Information Technologies from the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens and an Integrated MEng in Civil Engineering from the National Technical University of Athens. His research focuses mainly on LLM training, including multilingual corpus creation, data processing, synthetic data generation, post-training, inference, and evaluation. He has been responsible for the data pipelines behind Meltemi and Krikri, the first open Greek LLMs, and has contributed to several other projects such as Pharos, LLMs4EU, SciLake, ELRC3. Additionally, he has worked on machine translation, parallel corpus construction, and language resource development. His work has been published in venues including EMNLP, EAMT, WMT, and LREC.

Prokopis Prokopidis

Senior Research Fellow

Prokopis Prokopidis is a researcher and computational linguist at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) / Athena RC, where he has worked since 1998. He holds a degree in English Language and Literature from the University of Athens and an MA in Computational Linguistics from the University of Essex. He has participated in Greek and European projects focused on natural language processing, information extraction, and language resource development. He has contributed to the creation of annotated corpora, such as the Greek Dependency Treebank, as well as tools for automatic text annotation. His recent research includes named-entity recognition for archaeological texts, anonymization for court decisions, and the development of evaluation resources for Greek large language models. He has published in conferences, journals, and edited volumes.

Chara Tsoukala

Scientific Associate

Chara Tsoukala is a Research Associate at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) at Athena R.C. She holds an MSc in Human-Machine Communication from the University of Groningen and a PhD from Radboud University, where she investigated bilingual sentence production and code-switching through cognitive computational modeling. Her current research focuses on multilingual and low-resource language technologies, with particular emphasis on Automatic Speech Recognition for under-resourced languages, Natural Language Processing, and LLM-based agents and multi-agent systems.

Katerina Gkirtzou

Scientific Associate

Katerina Gkirtzou is a Scientific Associate at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) at Athena R.C. She holds a PhD in Applied Mathematics from École Centrale Paris, where she investigated sparsity regularization and graph-based representation in medical imaging. She has participated in designing and building major European infrastructures for language resources — including CLARIN:EL, the European Language Grid and Language Data Space. Her current research focuses on grounding language technology in structured knowledge, with particular emphasis on modelling lexical and linguistic resources as Linked Data (OntoLex/LLOD), knowledge graphs and neuro-symbolic methods.

George Paraskevopoulos

Alexandros Nousias

Research Associate

Alexandros Nousias is a Research Associate at the Institute of Informatics & Telecommunications of NCSR Demokritos, specialising in digital and AI law, governance, and ethics. He advises research organisations, corporates, and technology companies across both research and market-facing projects, and teaches AI ethics, law, and governance at postgraduate level in Greece. He promotes a shift from compliance as a minimum requirement to quality as the real foundation of trustworthy AI. He contributed to the “Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation” as Technical Consultant to the High-Level Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence to the Prime Minister. He is also involved in Pharos, the Greek AI Factory, focusing on compliance and governance. He also serves as Chair of the Greek JTC 21 Mirror Committee on European Harmonised Standards and is an IEEE CertifAIEd AI Ethics Lead Assessor.
